taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-14, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 161.1 | 3.39 | 3.39
2 | 1022.2 | 1.76 | 5.15
3 | 85.2 | 1.93 | 7.08
4 | 88.8 | 9.77 | 16.85
5 | 117.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-14, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-14, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model shows five layers. Resistivity decreases then increases across the sequence: Layer 1 (161.1 Ω·m) overlies a thin, highly resistive Layer 2 (1022.2 Ω·m), followed by a low-resistivity Layer 3 (85.2 Ω·m), a slightly higher Layer 4 (88.8 Ω·m), and a more resistive basal Layer 5 (117.4 Ω·m) presumed infinite.

Applying the curve-type rules to the four three-layer sets:
- Layers 1-2-3: r1<r2>r3 → K
- Layers 2-3-4: r2>r3<r4 → H
- Layers 3-4-5: r3<r4<r5 → A

This yields the sequence K-H-A, consistent with the on-file classification of KHA-type. The resistivity pattern (high resistive layer sandwiched between lower layers, followed by a gradual increase at depth) supports this curve type. No discrepancy was found between the layer data and the stated classification.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
